title: Herb-Crusted Baked Salmon Tray
seoTitle: Herb-Crusted Baked Salmon Tray | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Flaky fillets with dill, parsley, and roasted asparagus for the crew
subtitle: Flaky fillets with dill, parsley, and roasted asparagus for the crew
description: Salmon fillets bake on a sheet with a fresh herb crust, lemon, and asparagus spears. Designed for quick portioning and gentle hold in a low oven.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Herb-Crusted Baked Salmon Tray in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch salmon. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Preheat and prep asparagus
steps.instruction: Heat oven to 400°F. Toss asparagus with 1 tbsp olive oil and a pinch of salt until spears look lightly coated, not dripping. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Make herb crust paste
steps.instruction: Combine dill, parsley, garlic, lemon zest, Dijon, remaining olive oil, salt, and pepper into a thick paste that clings to fish. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Season salmon fillets
steps.instruction: Pat salmon dry. Spread herb paste evenly on flesh side of each fillet, pressing gently so it adheres during baking. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Bake until just opaque
steps.instruction: Place salmon on parchment-lined pans with asparagus alongside. Bake 12–16 minutes until thickest part reads 125–130°F and flakes with gentle pressure. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Finish with lemon and rest
steps.instruction: Top with lemon slices, rest 3 minutes off heat. Flesh should look opaque pink at center, not chalky or gray throughout. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

proTips: Pull salmon 5°F early—it keeps cooking on the hot tray during rest.
Buy center-cut fillets of similar thickness so nothing overcooks while waiting on thick pieces.
Wipe pans immediately after service; baked-on herb crust comes off easier when warm.
tonightSpread: Farro or brown rice pilaf with toasted almonds.
Cucumber-dill yogurt sauce for spooning over salmon.
leftovers: Flake cold salmon into a green salad with capers and red onion.
Salmon cakes next shift: mix flakes with egg, panko, and herbs, pan-sear until crisp.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Lean protein that feels like a treat. Cooks fast after calls and does not leave the kitchen smelling like fried fish.
mealPrepNotes: Pat fillets dry ahead and keep chilled. Mix herb topping in a squeeze bottle for fast application before baking. Station: Space fillets 2 inches apart so heat circulates and edges stay tender, not rubbery. Station: Use a fish spatula at the line to keep fillets intact during portioning. Station: Hold finished salmon at 150°F max—higher heat dries omega-3-rich fillets quickly.
